findings.title: Error IDs are paired with the wrong nodestore payloads
findings.body: `fetch_error_details()` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` (which returns a mapping keyed by node id and may omit/reorder missing keys), and then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. Any missing or re-ordered entry shifts the pairing, so an `ErrorEvent` can be created with the id of one error and the title/message/timestamp of another, producing wrong error text and wrong chronological placement in the Seer prompt. Iterate `events.items()` and map the node id back to the original event id instead of zipping the raw `values()`. The surrounding `except Exception: return []` also means this silently degrades to "no errors" rather than surfacing the problem.

findings.title: get_environment_info triggers a per-issue recommended-event lookup during PR comment generation
findings.body: `get_environment_info()` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for every issue included in a merged-PR comment. That helper performs a search/snuba query plus a nodestore fetch per issue, so generating a comment for the top 5 issues now issues up to 5 extra remote queries inside the webhook/task path that previously only read `issue.culprit` from the already-loaded model. This adds latency and external load to every PR comment, and the broad `except Exception` means failures are invisible apart from an info log. Consider batching the environment lookup (or deriving it from data already fetched for the issue list).

findings.title: New table widget path renders hardcoded empty data instead of query results
findings.body: When `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true, `TableWidgetVisualization` is rendered with `columns={[]}` and `tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}` while the actual `result` (fields, meta, data) is ignored. Any organization with that flag enabled will see completely blank dashboard tables instead of their widget data. The real `result`/`fields`/`datasetConfig` values need to be mapped into `TabularData`/`TabularColumn` before this branch is usable.

findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filter only applies while searching
findings.body: `sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns `sorted` early when `searchQuery` is empty, so the newly added `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` exclusion (`is_segment`, `project_id`, `received`) is only applied once the user types something. In the default (no search) state those attributes are still shown, which is the opposite of the intent and makes the list inconsistent as soon as a user starts/clears a search. The hidden-attribute filter should be applied to the base list, independently of the search term.

findings.title: Hook can now return undefined attributes where it previously always returned a TagCollection
findings.body: The hook was rewritten to return `attributes: isFetching ? previous : data` from `useQuery`. `data` is `undefined` whenever the query errors, is disabled (`enabled` false), or has not run, and `previous` is also `undefined` on the first render — whereas the old implementation always derived a concrete `TagCollection` object (`result.data ?? []` reduced into `{}`). Consumers that do `Object.keys(attributes)` or spread the value (e.g. the filter-key sections / search query builder tag collections) will throw on error or while the hook is disabled. Default to `{}` (or make the undefined case explicit for all callers).

findings.title: Attribute-keys query key omits the organization
findings.body: `queryKey` is `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]`, and `makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions` only contains item type, attribute type, project ids and the datetime range — the organization slug used to build the request URL is not part of the key. Two organizations with the same project ids/date range would share a cache entry, so attribute keys from one org can be served for another after an org switch within the same session. Include the organization slug (or the full URL) in the query key.

findings.title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check uses truthiness, so age=0 bypasses it
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` checks `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and `validate_age` checks `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. A report containing `age: 0` (a legitimate value for a report generated right now) together with a `timestamp` passes both validators, defeating the intended "exactly one of age/timestamp" rule; conversely `timestamp: 0` also slips through. Use `is not None`/`in self.initial_data` instead of truthiness.

findings.title: One invalid report rejects the entire batch
findings.body: The POST handler returns 422 for the whole request as soon as any single report in the array fails validation, discarding the valid reports in the same batch. Browsers send reports in batches and will keep retrying the same (permanently invalid) payload, so a single malformed report from one page permanently blocks collection of the rest of that batch. Consider skipping/counting invalid reports and still returning 200 for the valid ones.

findings.title: Coverage for the application/reports+json content type was removed
findings.body: The previous test posted with `content_type="application/reports+json"` (the content type browsers actually use for the Reporting API) and asserted the request body was logged. After the refactor every success-path test posts with the default content type, so `BrowserReportsJSONParser` — the only reason the custom parser class exists — is no longer exercised by any test. A regression in the parser media type would silently break real browser reports while the suite stays green.

findings.title: Analytics event recorded before feature check and request validation
findings.body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` is executed as the first statement of `post()`, before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check and before schema validation. Every request from orgs without the feature, and every malformed/polling request, is counted as an assemble event, so the metric does not reflect actual assemble attempts. Move the `record()` call after the feature gate (and ideally after validation).

findings.title: Custom cell renderers fall back on any falsy return, not just undefined
findings.body: Both `renderDefaultHeadCell` and `renderDefaultBodyCell` do `const cell = render...(); if (cell) return cell;`. The documented contract (see tableWidgetVisualization.stories.tsx and the prop JSDoc) is that returning `undefined` triggers the fallback renderer. With a truthiness check, a custom renderer that legitimately returns `null` (render nothing), `''`, or `0` will be silently replaced by the default renderer, which is not what the docs promise and is hard to debug. Compare against `undefined` explicitly.
